summary: One BLOCKER: migration 0309's prestate hard-pins the cluster-wide clara% role count at 18, and hosted carries 19 (clara_storage_docs) - proven by running the block verbatim against a hosted-shaped census in a rolled-back transaction, and the integrator's from-scratch proof on a disposable cluster cannot catch it. Three MAJORs: #933's wire schema imposes two length bounds the particulars door does not have, so a realistic 218-character asset description silently deletes the whole proposal; the successor contract reads a date column with no ::text cast, which node-postgres returns as a JS Date (measured: 2026-09-15 -> "2026-09-14T16:00:00.000Z" under Asia/Kuala_Lumpur), so v6 either drops every proposal or ships an off-by-one in-service date; and #871's attempts table is append-only with a DELETE-blocking trigger, no TRUNCATE and no retention, written once per request from a PUBLIC unauthenticated page render. findings.title: 0309's prestate hard-pins 18 clara% roles cluster-wide; HOSTED has 19, so the migration ABORTS in the release window
findings.evidence: packages/db/migrations/0309_invite_preview_public_door.sql:182-188 raises CLR10 unless `select count(*) from pg_roles where rolname like 'clara%'` is EXACTLY 18. Hosted is 19. Three independent sources: (a) docs/plan/active/riders-2026-09-20/RELEASE-W2-RUNBOOK.md step 3 pre-window reads - '14 differences, all role-level and all Supabase-only: ... clara_storage_docs and its two memberships exist only on hosted'; (b) RELEASE-W3-RUNBOOK.md repeats the same 14 env lines and asks the operator to re-count them; (c) packages/db/deploy/roles-bootstrap.sql:293, in the file THIS LANE edited, still reads 'Expect: 19 clara_% roles total (18 schema lanes + clara_storage_docs)'. MEASURED: on clara_l05, inside `begin; create role clara_storage_docs nologin noinherit; <0309 section-0(b) verbatim>; rollback;` the block printed 'hosted-shaped pre-0309 clara% census = 19' and then raised: 'ERROR: #871 prestate: expected 18 clara-prefixed roles before this file (0002/0006/0009/0121/0126/0160/0163), found 19 -- a cluster carrying leftovers from an earlier from-scratch chain needs scripts/role-census-reset.mjs first'. Post-rollback census re-read 20 / clara_storage_docs absent, so the lane database is untouched. The lane rig has NO clara_storage_docs (measured: 20 clara% roles, roster listed, that name absent), which is exactly why the lane never saw it. NOT precedent: the two other role-minting migrations assert role PRESENCE, never a count - 0160:57-59,119-122 and 0163:58-62,164-167; 0154:3788 is a TAIL 'this file mints no role' assertion that applied long before storage provisioning. The integrator's from-scratch chain runs on a disposable cluster, which has no clara_storage_docs, so that proof CANNOT catch this.
findings.impact: The hosted wave-4 migrate step stops at 0309 with an error message that sends the operator to scripts/role-census-reset.mjs - which on hosted would be the wrong and destructive thing to do. Everything after 0309 in the wave is blocked inside the window.
findings.required_fix: Replace the absolute census in section 0(b) with what 0160/0163 do: assert the roles this file mints are ABSENT and the roles it relies on are PRESENT. If an arithmetic census is wanted, exclude the known deploy-artifact roles (`and rolname <> 'clara_storage_docs'`, or `not in` the deploy roster) and say in the header that the count is over chain-minted roles only. The tail's T.4 (`v_n <> v_pre + 2`, lines 563-567) is already relative and needs no change.

findings.title: faParticularsProposalSchema invents two length bounds the particulars door does not have; a realistic asset description deletes the whole proposal, silently
findings.evidence: packages/runtime/lib/fa-particulars-proposal.ts:335 `description: z.string().trim().min(1).max(200).nullable()` and :337 `reason: z.string().max(400)`, under a header (:321-322) that claims 'Every bound here is clara._fa_validate_particulars's own (0041:2977-3033) - none is a rule of this module's'. FALSIFIED by reading packages/db/migrations/0041_wave_d_a_fa_register.sql:2977-3033: the validator imposes NO length bound on description and has no reason field at all; and clara.fixed_assets.description is `text NOT NULL` with character_maximum_length NULL (measured on clara_l05 via information_schema.columns) and carries no length CHECK. MEASURED by driving the real function: a 218-character vehicle description ('Toyota Hiace panel van, registration ..., chassis ..., purchased from ... under invoice ... dated 15 September 2026, fitted with refrigeration unit and rear shelving') -> deriveFaParticularsProposal returns description length 218 and faParticularsProposalSchema.safeParse(...) returns success:false. The reason is equally close to its ceiling: the client_knowledge branch with a single realistic recorded-policy label measured 395 of 400 characters; the retired_account_policy branch measured 346. reasonFor (:213-245) has no cap and deriveFaParticularsProposal never validates its own output. The report's own successor contract (wave4-lane05-ticket933.md section 5) then makes the consequence total: 'safeParse(proposal).success === false (a defect, not a refusal) -> treat as null and open the question without a block.'
findings.impact: For exactly the assets whose descriptions are long - document-derived plant and vehicle rows, i.e. the ones a person most wants help with - #933's whole deliverable disappears. No log, no refusal, no evidence: the person sees today's empty form and nobody can tell it apart from 'no ground was found'. The same happens to any asset whose account code or recorded-policy label pushes the reason past 400.
findings.required_fix: Either drop the two bounds the door does not have, or make the producer honour them: truncate description to 200 in deriveFaParticularsProposal and cap reasonFor's output (the fixed tail alone is ~135 characters). Add one cell per bound that drives the real function with an over-length input and asserts a block that still parses. Correct the header sentence either way.

findings.title: The successor contract reads fa.acquired_date with no ::text cast; node-postgres hands back a JS Date, so v6 either drops every proposal or ships an off-by-one Asia/Kuala_Lumpur in-service date
findings.evidence: docs/plan/active/riders-2026-09-20/reports/wave4-lane05-ticket933.md, successor contract section 3: the new step's SQL (a) is `select fa.asset_account_code, fa.acquired_date, (...) as particulars_complete from clara.fixed_assets fa where ...` and the mapping takes acquiredDate straight from it, with no cast and no note. MEASURED with the repo's own pg 8.20.0 against clara_l05: `select '2026-09-15'::date as d` returns [object Date], JSON.stringify "2026-09-14T16:00:00.000Z" (the host is Asia/Kuala_Lumpur, so the Date is local midnight and its UTC spelling is the PREVIOUS calendar day); /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(value) is false; the same column with an explicit ::text returns the string '2026-09-15'. No setTypeParser exists anywhere in the repo source (only inside packages/runtime/.output's vendored pg). Consequences in the shipped code: faParticularsProposalSchema :334 `start_date: z.string().regex(...)` rejects a Date, so by the contract's own section 5 the WHOLE proposal is dropped; and prettyDate (:192-198) fails its regex and returns the Date unchanged, so the reason line would read 'I propose Tue Sep 15 2026 00:00:00 GMT+0800 ... as the in-service date'. No precedent protects the transcriber: v4's own loadPendingFixedAssetStepV4 (packages/runtime/workflows/claraWork.v4.impl.ts:691-732) deliberately selects NO date column, so this is the first date read on this path.
findings.impact: The one artifact the lane was asked to write 'in full so that cut is transcription, not design' contains the transcription trap. Transcribed as written, v6 opens every question with no proposal at all. Transcribed with the obvious repair (.toISOString().slice(0,10)), the in-service date is one day earlier than the acquisition's Asia/Kuala_Lumpur posting date - a wrong date recorded under a person's signature, on a driver that determines every depreciation charge from then on.
findings.required_fix: Change the contract's SQL (a) to `fa.acquired_date::text as acquired_date`, state in the mapping that acquiredDate is a YYYY-MM-DD Asia/Kuala_Lumpur calendar string and never a Date, and add the same line to FaProposalAsset.acquiredDate's doc comment. A cell that drives the derivation with a Date and asserts it is refused (rather than silently mis-shaped) would pin it.

findings.kind: unbounded-growth / self-perpetuating-lockout from an unauthenticated public URL
findings.title: Every call - including a refused one - writes an unprunable row to clara.invite_preview_attempts, and the writer is a public page GET
findings.evidence: 0309 section C inserts the evidence row BEFORE either window is evaluated (migration lines ~357-366), so a rate_limited answer still costs a row. MEASURED on clara_l05 through the real door under `set role clara_invite_preview`: twelve sequential calls on one token with a fresh address each time returned [preview x5, rate_limited(900s) x7] and left 12 rows for that token - every refused call counted, and retry_after_seconds stayed pinned at the 900-second ceiling from the sixth call on, so sustained traffic holds the token limb shut indefinitely. The table cannot be pruned: MEASURED inside a rolled-back transaction, `set role clara_fn_owner; delete from clara.invite_preview_attempts where attempted_at < now() - interval '15 minutes'` raises 'ERROR: invite_preview_attempts is append-only' - clara._tf_append_only() is an unconditional raise (prosrc read off the live catalog) and TRUNCATE is blocked too. There is no retention job (0309's own header says so). The writer is reached without any authentication: apps/web/app/(entry)/invite/[token]/page.tsx:107-114 calls readPublicInvitePreview on every render of /invite/:token?ct=..., a route the page's own header records as public ('proxy.ts allowlists "/invite"'). 0163's clara.confirmation_attempts has the same table shape but is reached from a form POST, not a page GET.
findings.impact: (a) An unauthenticated flood of a public URL grows an append-only, unprunable table one row plus two index entries per request, forever; (b) anyone holding an invite link (a forwarded e-mail, a retrying client, a crawler) can keep a real invitee's preview permanently walled, because each refused reload slides the window forward; (c) the retention follow-up the report proposes ('one small lane could give both a retention job') CANNOT be written as a job - it needs a migration that drops or conditions the append-only trigger, which the follow-up does not say.
findings.required_fix: At minimum, correct the follow-up to name the trigger as part of the work, and say in 0309's header that the table is unprunable as shipped. Better within this lane: skip the INSERT once the window is already over the ceiling (count first, insert only when admitting), which both stops the self-perpetuating lockout and bounds the table at 5 rows per key per window; or give the trigger a `when (current_user <> 'clara_fn_owner')` condition so a retention lane is possible at all.

findings.title: A null asset_account_code makes the sibling and retired-policy grounds accept EVERY account, while the knowledge ground correctly does not
findings.evidence: packages/runtime/lib/fa-particulars-proposal.ts:170 `if (asset.assetAccount !== null && s.assetAccount !== asset.assetAccount) continue;` - when the pending row's account is null the filter is skipped entirely and siblings from any account ground the proposal. :287 does the same for the retired policy: `retired !== null && (asset.assetAccount === null || retired.assetAccount === asset.assetAccount)`. The knowledge arm (:273-275) is written correctly: with a null account only a firm-wide note (note.assetAccount === null) qualifies. clara.fixed_assets.asset_account_code is nullable (measured: information_schema.columns, is_nullable = YES), so the state is representable. reasonFor :244 then prints 'Every other completed asset on this asset account is depreciated <drivers>, so I propose the same' - a claim about an account the ground did not come from.
findings.impact: Latent rather than live: the lane's own successor SQL (b) filters `fa.asset_account_code = $3::text`, which yields nothing when $3 is null, so v6 as contracted never enters the widened branch. But deriveFaParticularsProposal is an exported pure function with a documented input type, and the three arms disagreeing about the same null is exactly the kind of inconsistency a later caller inherits.
findings.required_fix: Make the three arms agree: with a null asset.assetAccount, ground only on inputs whose own account is also null, or ground on nothing. One cell driving assetAccount: null with a sibling on account '1500' pins it.

findings.title: Disagreeing knowledge notes silently pick the first, while disagreeing siblings correctly ground nothing; and residualCents is carried by all three ground types and read by none
findings.evidence: packages/runtime/lib/fa-particulars-proposal.ts:29 states the rule - a split account 'grounds nothing and says so: picking a side would be Clara choosing between two humans' judgements' - and fromSiblings :177-181 honours it. The knowledge loop :278-281 (`if (knowledgeNote === null || (scoped && knowledgeNote.assetAccount === null))`) takes the FIRST admissible note and never compares it with a later one, so two conflicting records recorded by two people resolve by array order. Separately, FaProposalSibling.residualCents, FaProposalKnowledgeNote.residualCents and FaProposalRetiredPolicy.residualCents (:83, :113, :125) are never read: congruent() (:153-163) takes only method/life/rate and the proposal always sets residual_cents: 0 (:308). So siblings whose residuals differ still 'agree', and reasonFor :244 says 'so I propose the same' about a set of drivers that is not the same.
findings.impact: The knowledge ground is unfed on this frontier (the module's own :90-99 records that clara.knowledge_keys catalogues no depreciation key - the FK premise stands), so the first-wins path is not live today. The residual half IS live through the sibling ground: a retired policy or an account precedent carrying a non-nil residual is half-adopted, with only the generic 'a nil residual, which is this firm's default' tail disclosing it.
findings.required_fix: Give the knowledge arm the same disagreement rule as siblings. Either read residualCents on the grounds that carry it, or delete the field from the three input types and say in the header that the residual is always the firm default.

findings.title: role-census-reset.test.mjs now asserts on the migration NUMBER, the anti-pattern the lane's own gate module forbids in the same commit range
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/role-census-reset.test.mjs (new lines) asserts `roles.every((r) => /^(01(60|63)|0309)_/.test(r.file))`. packages/db/tests/invite-preview-public-preintegration-gate.mjs, added by the same ticket, states the rule it breaks: 'THE STEM, NEVER THE NUMBER ... never off ^0309_, because numbers are claimed at merge and a number-keyed probe turns every cell into a silent green SKIP the moment the integrator renumbers this file (adversarial ADV-L10-04, 2026-09-20).' 0309 is currently unique across the wave-4 reports visible from the main checkout (0301, 0302, 0303, 0305, 0309, 0310, 0311, 0316), so the risk is renumbering, not collision.
findings.impact: Here it fails LOUDLY rather than skipping, so it is a stop rather than a hole - but it is one more file the integrator must remember to edit if 0309 moves.
findings.required_fix: Key the assertion on the file STEM (/_invite_preview_public_door\.sql$/ beside the two existing stems), not on the number.

findings.title: The successor contract's particulars_complete is narrower than v4's own 'should I ask?' predicate
findings.evidence: Contract SQL (a) derives particulars_complete as `(fa.depreciation_start_date is not null and fa.depreciation_method is not null)`. v4's loadPendingFixedAssetStepV4 (claraWork.v4.impl.ts:703-714) additionally requires `residual_cents is not null` for straight_line and reducing_balance. Where they disagree, v4 opens the question and deriveFaParticularsProposal returns null (:256), so the question opens with no proposal. ck_fa_method_drivers (measured on clara_l05) rules out most half-states, and clara._fa_validate_particulars coalesces the residual to 0 for both depreciating methods, so I could NOT prove the divergent state reachable - stating it as a divergence, not as a live defect.
findings.required_fix: Spell particulars_complete in the contract with v4's own predicate, or say in the contract why the narrower one is deliberate.

findings.title: What I tried to break and could not - recorded so the next reviewer does not repeat it
findings.evidence: RACE: six genuinely concurrent pg Clients, each `set role clara_invite_preview`, all calling the door with ONE token and ONE origin digest -> ['preview','preview','preview','preview','preview','rate_limited'], 5 served / 1 walled / 0 threw, 6 attempt rows. No TOCTOU. LOCK ORDER: both branches of 0309's advisory-lock block acquire in ascending numeric order (token<=origin: token then origin, with the equal case de-duplicated; else origin then token), so no cross-call cycle exists; a 64-bit collision only over-serializes. EXISTENCE ORACLE: the sixth call on a real token and the sixth on invented tokens both returned {"outcome":"rate_limited","retry_after_seconds":900} byte for byte; the wall runs before the lookup on every arm, so an unknown token costs exactly what a real one costs. DOOR DRIFT: sha256(convert_to(btrim(p_token), 'UTF8')) is byte-identical in clara.preview_invite, clara.accept_invite and clara.preview_invite_by_token, and the mask tail `|| '***@' || substr(inv.email, v_at + 1)` is byte-identical in both preview doors (read off pg_proc.prosrc on the live catalog). RETRY-AFTER ARITHMETIC: `offset v_count - 4` is correct given the just-inserted row counts toward future windows (need (v_count+1)-4 rows to expire; the last of those is 0-based index v_count-4). GATES RE-RUN by me, not taken from the report: `node --test --test-concurrency=1 $GATES tests/invite-preview-public.test.mjs tests/fa-particulars-proposal.test.mjs` -> 17 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped; `node --import ./test/bootstrap.mjs --import tsx --test` over the five new web files -> 24 pass / 0 fail. TENANT ISOLATION: #933 adds no write and its one new read (loadAssetParticularsProposal) leans on clara_authenticated's forced-RLS p_agent_interruptions_human = (firm_id = clara.jwt_firm()), which the lane's own p933.read.firm_walled drives and which re-ran green. All reviewer probe files were removed; `git status --short` in the worktree is empty.
